questions.question: As you approach a blind intersection, where should you position your motorcycle in the lane?

options.text: In the position where other drivers can see you earliest.
Close to the traffic control device.
At the outside edge of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the position where other drivers can see you earliest.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, move to where other drivers can see you as soon as possible.

questions.question: How should you swerve on a motorcycle?

options.text: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn the handlebars quickly.
Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve away from danger, push on the handgrip on the side where you want to go.

questions.question: Small vehicles appear to be ________ and slower than they really are.

options.text: Closer
Farther away
Larger

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away
questions.explanation: Small vehicles like motorcycles are hard to judge. Other drivers may misjudge how fast you are going and where you are located.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn
No left turn
No U-turn

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn
questions.explanation: This white sign with red and black markings tells drivers that U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What is the best way to help others see your motorcycle?

options.text: Use your headlight.
Weave in your lane.
Maintain eye contact with other road users.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your headlight.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on. This is the best way to help other drivers see you. Always check that your headlight works before you ride.

questions.question: What is the best footwear for motorcycle riders?

options.text: Sneakers
Leather boots
Sandals

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather boots
questions.explanation: Leather boots give the best protection. They should be high and strong enough to protect and support your ankles.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield
Slow-moving vehicle
Railroad crossing

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle
questions.explanation: This sign is placed on vehicles moving slower than 25 mph, such as farm equipment, construction machinery, or horse-drawn vehicles.

questions.question: When can a motorcycle pass on the right?

options.text: If there is at least eight feet of clear pavement.
By riding on the shoulder of the road.
By riding on the grass, if it is level.

questions.correctAnswerText: If there is at least eight feet of clear pavement.
questions.explanation: You may pass on the right only if there is at least eight feet of clear pavement to the right of the vehicle ahead. Never leave the road to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: What can a plastic face shield protect you from?

options.text: Noise.
Dust.
Glare.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dust.
questions.explanation: A face shield protects your face during a crash. It also protects you from rocks thrown by other vehicles, wind, dust, dirt, rain, and insects.

questions.question: What should you remember when riding near a truck?

options.text: If you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.
You should not be able to see the truck's mirrors.
You should focus on your motorcycle and ignore the truck's mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.
questions.explanation: Stay out of the blind spots of large trucks. If you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.

questions.question: What is one difference between goggles and a windshield?

options.text: Goggles protect your eyes from wind, but a windshield does not.
A windshield protects your eyes from wind, but goggles do not.
A windshield stops your eyes from watering better than goggles do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Goggles protect your eyes from wind, but a windshield does not.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes from wind, but most windshields do not. A windshield is not a good substitute for goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: What is a main cause of single-vehicle motorcycle crashes?

options.text: Riders going too fast for the weather conditions.
Riders turning too wide in a curve or turn.
Riders leaving the road while trying to avoid hitting another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders turning too wide in a curve or turn.
questions.explanation: A main cause of single-vehicle crashes is when riders turn too wide in a curve or turn. Turning too wide can cause a motorcycle to leave the road or hit an object.

questions.question: Under normal riding conditions, what is one of the best ways to help others see your motorcycle?

options.text: Flash your lights.
Keep your high beam headlight on.
Paint your motorcycle a dark color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your high beam headlight on.
questions.explanation: The best way to help others see your motorcycle is to keep your headlight on (and your running lights if you have them). Use your high beam headlight day and night whenever it is legal and safe.

questions.question: If you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle, what should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
You should flash your headlight to tell the other vehicle to go.
You should continue through the intersection and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: If you reach an intersection without signs or traffic lights at the same time as another driver, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: Where is there the greatest risk of conflict between you and other vehicles?

options.text: At an intersection
On the highway
On any road

questions.correctAnswerText: At an intersection
questions.explanation: The greatest risk of conflict between a motorcycle and other vehicles is at intersections.

questions.question: When sitting on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Use your arms to hold up your body.
Sit at an angle so your arms can support your weight.
Sit so you can use your arms to control the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit so you can use your arms to control the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Sit in a position that lets you use your arms to control the motorcycle. Do not sit in a way that requires your arms to hold up your body.

questions.question: If another driver makes eye contact with you:

options.text: You know they have seen you.
It does not always mean they have actually seen you.
They will properly yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not always mean they have actually seen you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume that eye contact means a driver has seen you. Drivers often look directly at motorcycles without actually noticing them.

questions.question: You should increase your following distance if:

options.text: It is raining.
There is light traffic.
It is sunny.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is raining.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance if it takes longer to stop, if you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, or if traffic is heavy and other vehicles may cut in front of you.

questions.question: Your motorcycle is weaving while riding over bridge gratings. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get over the surface faster.
Ride in a zigzagging pattern.
Keep a steady speed and ride straight across the gratings.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a steady speed and ride straight across the gratings.
questions.explanation: If your motorcycle weaves while riding over bridge gratings, keep a steady speed and go straight across. Zigzagging to stay in your lane is dangerous.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will enter the roadway.
A signal is ahead.
Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. You must come to a complete stop, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, and proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: When someone is passing you, where should you ride?

options.text: In the left part of the lane.
In the center of the lane.
In the right part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. This is safest. Riding on the side closer to the other driver increases crash risk. Riding on the far side may encourage them to move back too quickly.

questions.question: What should eye protection do?

options.text: Is not needed if your motorcycle has a windshield.
Is only needed in bad weather.
Lets you see clearly to both sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets you see clearly to both sides.
questions.explanation: Eye or face protection is required by law in California. Good protection covers your whole face during a crash. Your eye or face shield must let you see clearly to both sides.

questions.question: How should you sit to properly control a motorcycle?

options.text: Let your feet hang off the footrests.
Use your arms to hold up your body.
Keep your knees against the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can easily reach all controls. Keep your arms slightly bent and use them to steer. Press your knees against the gas tank to stay balanced during turns.

questions.question: How should a parked motorcycle be positioned against the curb?

options.text: At an angle of 45 to 90 degrees from the curb.
With no wheel or fender touching the curb.
Parallel to the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: At an angle of 45 to 90 degrees from the curb.
questions.explanation: Park your motorcycle at an angle of 45 to 90 degrees from the curb. One wheel or fender should touch the curb.

questions.question: What should a passenger do while riding?

options.text: Hold onto the rider's hips, waist, or belt.
Never hold onto the rider.
Not lean into any turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold onto the rider's hips, waist, or belt.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to grip your hips, waist, or belt firmly. They can also hold secure handholds if available.
